card.name: Maypole Dance
card.tagline: The Northern European spring rite — dancers weave coloured ribbons around the maypole, an unbroken pre-Christian ritual now embraced from Stockholm to Wellington.
card.profile: The maypole dance is the pre-Christian Northern European spring ritual where dancers — each holding a coloured ribbon attached to the top of a tall pole — weave in and out of formation in opposite directions, braiding the ribbons into geometric patterns down the pole's length. The tradition is most strongly maintained in Sweden (where Midsummer's Eve in late June is the national high holiday and the maypole — majstång — is raised in every village), Germany, England, and the Czech Republic. The maypole survives wherever Northern European descendants settled — the German diaspora in Texas, the English in Australia and New Zealand, the Swedes in Minnesota.
card.insight: Sweden's Midsommarafton — Midsummer's Eve — is the country's most widely celebrated national holiday, when virtually every Swedish village raises its majstång (maypole) and the population dances the small frogs dance (Små Grodorna) around it. The combination of summer-solstice daylight (the sun barely sets in central Sweden in late June) and centuries-old ritual makes Swedish Midsummer one of the most photographed traditional celebrations in Europe.
